title: Localization coordinates of the unaugmented ordered Cech sections
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$ a finite family with $\operatorname{span}(f)=I$. Let $L_f$ be the actual unaugmented ordered Cech section complex of the structure module on $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\setminus V(I)$, with scalars restricted to $A$, and let $b:A\to L_f^0$ be the restriction map, as in [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-ordered-cech-construction]. There exist $A$-linear isomorphisms $E_q:L_f^q\cong\prod_{t:\operatorname{Fin}(q+1)\hookrightarrow_o\operatorname{Fin}(r)}A_{\prod_i f(t(i))}$ for every $q\ge0$, using the localizations of [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $A$-algebra maps $l_{q,t,j}$ from the localization of the face deleting $j$ to that of $t$, such that $E_0(b(a))_t$ is the image of $a$ and $E_{q+1}(dx)_t=\sum_j(-1)^j l_{q,t,j}((E_qx)_{t\setminus j})$. Empty families, zero and repeated generators, and the zero ring are allowed. This is a statement about the unaugmented sections, without a cone, inverse rotation, or augmentation projection.

proof.text: Every generator belongs to I. The image in Spec A of an ordered intersection in U is the principal open of the product: membership is equivalent to every factor lying outside the prime ideal. Containment in U follows by taking any one factor, since the tuple has q+1 entries. This also handles the empty generating family, where there are no tuples.

On that principal open the structure-ring sections are a localization. Transport the canonical A-algebra equivalence between localizations along the equality of opens. Restriction of the structural ring map agrees with the algebra map from A; hence this ring equivalence is linear for the actual twice-restricted scalar action. Take the product of these equivalences.

Define each face algebra map by conjugating the actual restriction ring homomorphism through the face and full-intersection ring equivalences. Functoriality of restriction proves that the map commutes with A. In each signed summand, the inverse face equivalence cancels its forward equivalence. Additivity and integer linearity then identify the alternating differential.

Use the extension-by-zero term isomorphisms to pass from the natural-indexed ordered complex to its integer extension. The extend_d_eq identity cancels the successive term isomorphisms. The definition of alternatingCechZero cancels the inverse term isomorphism in degree zero, leaving precisely restriction of the structural map from A.

theorem ringComplexOrderedCech_sections_coordinates (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (I : Ideal A)
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    let L := ringComplexOrderedCechSections A I f
    ∃ (e : ∀ q : ℕ, (L.X (q : ℤ)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[A]
            ((t : Fin (q + 1) ↪o Fin r) → Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))))
          (l : ∀ (q : ℕ) (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r) (j : Fin (q + 2)),
            Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j i))) →ₐ[A]
              Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))),
          (∀ (x : A) (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin r),
            e 0 ((ringComplexOrderedCechFirst A I f).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
              algebraMap A (Localization.Away (∏ i, f (t i))) x) ∧
          (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : (L.X (q : ℤ)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
            (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r),
            e (q + 1) ((L.d (q : ℤ) ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.app
              (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
              ∑ j : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
                l q t j (e q x ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t)))
